chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Suleyman ibn Rushayd, from his father, from Bashir, who said:
I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The good life is in the spaciousness of the home, and the graciousness regarding the servants'.

key_terms.الْعَيْشُ: Life, livelihood, or way of living

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on the relationship between home size, servants, and quality of life?
ai.summary: In this concise tradition from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him), the concept of 'al-'aysh' (livelihood/prosperity) is explicitly linked to the physical spaciousness of one's dwelling, reflecting the Shia emphasis on domestic environment as a determinant of quality of life. Simultaneously, 'al-fadl' (nobility or distinction) is defined not by wealth alone, but by the dignified treatment of servants, elevating domestic ethics to a marker of spiritual and social status. This hadith is often cited in discussions on Islamic architecture and social hierarchy, illustrating how material conditions and moral conduct are intertwined in achieving a blessed life.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from his father, from Bashir who said,
‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The good life is in the spaciousness of the home, and the graciousness regarding the servants’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Nuh ibn Shu’ayb from Sulayman ibn Rashid from his father from Bashir who has said the following: “
I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Spaciousness of the house and extra help from the servants are of the means of happy living.’”
